private final ListDataProvider manufacturerDataProvider; @Inject ManufacturerView( Binder uiBinder) { initManufacturerGrid(); initWidget(uiBinder.createAndBindUi(this)); manufacturerDataProvider = new ListDataProvider<>(); } @Override public void replaceManufacturer(ManufacturerDto oldManufacturer, ManufacturerDto newManufacturer) { List manufacturerDtos = manufacturerDataProvider.getList(); int index = manufacturerDtos.indexOf(oldManufacturer); manufacturerDtos.add(index, newManufacturer); manufacturerDtos.remove(index + 1); } @UiHandler("create") void onCreateClicked(ClickEvent ignored) { getUiHandlers().onCreate(); } private void initManufacturerGrid() { manufacturerGrid = new CellTable<>(); manufacturerGrid.setSelectionModel(new NoSelectionModel()); initDataColumns(); initActionColumns(); } private void initDataColumns() { Column idColumn = new Column(new NumberCell()) { @Override public Long getValue(ManufacturerDto manufacturerDto) { return manufacturerDto.getId(); } }; Column nameColumn = new Column(new TextCell()) { @Override public String getValue(ManufacturerDto manufacturerDto) { return manufacturerDto.getName(); } }; manufacturerGrid.addColumn(idColumn, "ID"); manufacturerGrid.addColumn(nameColumn, "Name"); manufacturerGrid.setColumnWidth(idColumn, 50, Unit.PX); } private void initActionColumns() { Cell editCell = new ActionCell<>("Edit", new Delegate() { @Override public void execute(ManufacturerDto manufacturerDto) { getUiHandlers().onEdit(manufacturerDto); } }); Cell deleteCell = new ActionCell<>("Delete", new Delegate() { @Override public void execute(ManufacturerDto manufacturerDto) { Boolean confirm = Window.confirm("Are you sure you want to delete " + manufacturerDto.getName() + "?"); if (confirm) { getUiHandlers().onDelete(manufacturerDto); } } }); IdentityColumn editColumn = new IdentityColumn<>(editCell); IdentityColumn deleteColumn = new IdentityColumn<>(deleteCell); manufacturerGrid.addColumn(editColumn, "Edit"); manufacturerGrid.addColumn(deleteColumn, "Delete"); manufacturerGrid.setColumnWidth(editColumn, 75, Unit.PX); manufacturerGrid.setColumnWidth(deleteColumn, 75, Unit.PX); } } package com.gwtplatform.carstore.client.application.manufacturer; public class ManufacturerPresenter extends Presenter implements ManufacturerUiHandlers, ActionBarEvent.ActionBarHandler { interface MyView extends View, HasUiHandlers { void addManufacturer(ManufacturerDto manufacturerDto); void displayManufacturers(List manufacturerDtos); void removeManufacturer(ManufacturerDto manufacturerDto); void replaceManufacturer(ManufacturerDto oldManufacturer, ManufacturerDto newManufacturer); } @ProxyCodeSplit @NameToken(NameTokens.MANUFACTURER) interface MyProxy extends ProxyPlace { } private final PlaceManager placeManager; private final ResourceDelegate manufacturersDelegate; private final EditManufacturerPresenter editManufacturerPresenter; private ManufacturerDto editingManufacturer; @Inject ManufacturerPresenter( EventBus eventBus, MyView view, MyProxy proxy, PlaceManager placeManager, ResourceDelegate manufacturersDelegate, EditManufacturerPresenter editManufacturerPresenter) { super(eventBus, view, proxy, ApplicationPresenter.SLOT_MAIN_CONTENT); this.placeManager = placeManager; this.manufacturersDelegate = manufacturersDelegate; this.editManufacturerPresenter = editManufacturerPresenter; getView().setUiHandlers(this); } @Override public void onActionEvent(ActionBarEvent event) { if (event.getActionType() == ActionType.ADD && event.isTheSameToken(NameTokens.getManufacturer())) { placeManager.revealPlace(new Builder().nameToken(NameTokens.getDetailManufacturer()).build()); } } @Override public void onDetail(ManufacturerDto manufacturerDto) { PlaceRequest placeRequest = new Builder().nameToken(NameTokens.getDetailManufacturer()) .with("id", String.valueOf(manufacturerDto.getId())) .build(); placeManager.revealPlace(placeRequest); } @Override public void onEdit(ManufacturerDto manufacturerDto) { editingManufacturer = manufacturerDto; editManufacturerPresenter.edit(manufacturerDto); } @Override public void onCreate() { editingManufacturer = null; The Angular app now covers the Manufacturers, Ratings and Reports screens, the header menubar and the success/error messages. `npx ng build` succeeds. I did not run the Cucumber/Selenium suite; there is no Selenium or chromedriver in the environment. Instead I drove the app in headless Chromium over the DevTools protocol, served by `sh backend/run.sh` against the real REST API. That script exercised the same actions and selectors as the scenarios:

- **Manufacturers:**
  - The create popup opens and Close leaves the row count unchanged.
  - Save adds a row at the end and shows a success message containing "saved".
  - Editing the first row updates it.
  - Delete removes the row, after the `window.confirm()`.
- **Ratings:**
  - The create popup lists the cars. Entering 10 and saving adds a row, closes the popup and shows a success message.
  - Delete removes the row.
- **Reports:**
  - After the rating changes, the averages came out right: Ford 6 = (2 + 10) / 2, Mitsubishi 3.5.

The element ids, table layout and hash routing follow the acceptance criteria:

- The tables carry `gwt-debug-manufacturers`, `gwt-debug-ratings` and `gwt-debug-reports`, with `<thead>` headers named as in the GWT columns. Edit and Delete are the last two columns, or just Delete on Ratings.
- The popup controls, create buttons and messages use the matching `gwt-debug-…` ids.
- The menubar (`gwt-debug-menubar`) has links to `#/manufacturer`, `#/rating` and `#/report`, and the default route redirects to manufacturer.
- Messages auto-close after 5 seconds and have a close "X".

Two things you might trip over:

- **Hash URLs:** Angular's hash routing produces URLs like `#/manufacturer`, not `#manufacturer`. The menubar link `href`s still contain the GWT tokens, which is what the page objects check. I found no step in `e2e/` that waits on `#<token>` in the URL (the login and navigation steps aren't in the e2e sources), so I left it.
- **Message text:** Messages read "Manufacturer saved." and "Rating saved." I wrote those myself, because I did not look up the GWT message bundle.

The code is under `src/app/`.

I could not run the real Cucumber/Selenium suite here, so "every scenario in `e2e/` passes" is not proven.

**Why it can't run:**
- There is no chromedriver, and Selenium Manager needs network access.
- `e2e/` has no `pom.xml`, base `StepDefs`, Guice modules or `TestParameters`.
- The "I'm logged in" and "I navigate to the … page" steps are not defined anywhere in the sources. Login is out of scope and the REST API is unprotected, so the app has no login to perform.

**What I ran instead:** Headless Chromium against `sh backend/run.sh`, using real mouse events at each element's centre. An overlay covering a button would have blocked the click, and none did. The script followed the scenarios' selectors and flows:
- **Manufacturers:** Create then Close leaves the row count unchanged. Create then Save appends the row as the last one and shows a "saved" message. Editing the first row changes its name. Deleting removes the first row, after a stubbed `confirm`.
- **Ratings:** The create popup opens. Typing 10 and saving adds one row, closes the popup and shows a success message. Deleting removes the first row.
- **Reports:** The page shows the per-manufacturer averages. On a fresh datastore they matched my hand calculation (Ford 6 and Mitsubishi 3.5 after a 10 was added).
- **Menubar:** The links navigate with hash routing, and their hrefs contain `manufacturer`, `rating` and `report`.

**Shared datastore:** All three features run against one datastore, and the Manufacturers feature deletes the first manufacturer (Honda). Ratings for its cars then display as just an id, because the car has no manufacturer. In that state the Reports step `ReportPage.addRating` would fail on `car.indexOf('/')`. My repeated runs hit this: after Honda was deleted, the report came back empty and the labels turned into ids. This follows how the GWT table renders the car, so I left it. The e2e harness needs a freshly seeded datastore for the Reports feature, which `run.sh` provides on each start.

The Angular code is in `src/app/` and `npx ng build` succeeds.

Stop hook feedback:
[`npx ng build` succeeds; and served at http://localhost:8888/ng/ by `sh backend/run.sh`, the Angular app implements the Manufacturers, Ratings and Reports screens, the header menubar and the success/error messages so that every scenario in e2e/ (Manufacturers, Ratings and Reports features) works against the real REST API, with the element ids, table layout, hash routing and delete confirmation the task's acceptance criteria require.]: The e2e/ suite (Cucumber/Selenium) was never run; the assistant states "I could not run the real Cucumber/Selenium suite here, so 'every scenario in e2e/ passes' is not proven." The "I'm logged in" and "I navigate to the … page" steps are acknowledged as undefined, and the assistant's own ad-hoc Chromium script showed the Reports scenario failing after the Manufacturers feature deleted Honda ("the report came back empty and the labels turned into ids"). Build success and serving at /ng/ are shown, but full e2e scenario satisfaction is not.
The hook is right that this isn't proven, and the dirty-datastore failure is something I can make more robust. I'll look at what the API returns after the first manufacturer is deleted.
